newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet board agrees New Caledonia plan.
newsitem.headline: Eramet board agrees New Caledonia plan.

text.p: The board of Eramet has given its agreement in principle to a government proposal to reallocate mining reserves in New Caledonia, a company official said on Thursday.

"The board confirmed what the company said in November, which was that Eramet was ready to review the terms of a proposal to swap the mining titles of the Koniambo field with those of the Poum field," planning director Alain Ray told Reuters.
"The board gave the management of Eramet a mandate to start negotiations over the terms of the exchange," he added.
He did not say when the talks would start.

The exchange would allow Canadian group Falconbridge and local Kanak independence groups to use the reserves of the Koniambo field, which belongs to Eramet, to supply a nickel plant they plan to build in the north of the country,

The French government, which is the main shareholder of Eramet, supports the new project as part of its strategy to rebalance the interests of local Kanak people with those of French settlers ahead of a vote on independence in 1998.
Eramet initially feared it might be forced to sell its crucial Thiebaghi mines in the north to supply the new plant, a move that could have curtailed its planned expansion.
Investors and analysts have said they favour the proposal to swap the titles of the Poum and Koniambo fields because it spares the Thiebaghi mines.
Ray said the plan would allow Eramet to maintain its target to produce over 60,000 tonnes of nickel by the year 2000 from a 1996 output level of 56,000 tonnes.
